Kerala - A Case Study 
 
Achievements 
 
7.27 About the PDS System in the State, the Government of Kerala in their written 
replies furnished information as under:  
 
“Kerala has been a pioneer in the modernization of the Public Distribution 
System (PDS) by leveraging technology to enhance transparency and 
efficiency. The state's approach has focused on building a robust technical 
database and an integrated digital infrastructure. 
 
The Technical Database 
Kerala's PDS modernization began with the digitization of ration cards and 
beneficiary data. It is a key component of the state's e -governance initiatives, 
allowing for the generation of various reports, data sharing with other 
government departments, and secure citizen access to their data. 
 
The technical database is the foundation for several key applications: 
 
• Ration Card Management System (RCMS):  This is a client -server 
application that provides a workflow -based solution for all citizen services 
related to ration cards. This includes issuing new cards, adding or deleting 
members, and splitting cards. 
 
• Integrated Management of Public Distribution System (IMPDS):  Kerala 
has been at the forefront of modernizing its Public Distribution System 
(PDS) and has successfully integrated with the national iMPDS (Integrated 
Management of Public Distribution System) platform. The state's efforts are 
a crucial part of the "One Nation, One Ration Card" (ONORC) scheme, 
which aims to provide food security for all, including its non -native 
population. 
 
• Supply Chain Management System (SCMS):  Supply Chain Management 
System is a critical technological component that has been implemented to 
ensure the efficient, transparent, and end -to-end management of food 
grains from the time they are procured , to the moment they are distributed 
to beneficiaries. Kerala's SCMS is a digital backbone that ensures that the 
state's food security programs are not just efficient but also transparent and 
accountable. It is a vital tool that complements other technological 
initiatives like e -RCMS and AePDS, making Kerala a leader in PDS 
modernization. 
 
• Vehicle Tracking and Fleet Management System (VTFMS):  Vehicle 
Tracking and Fleet Management System is a crucial technological initiative 
implemented by the Kerala Civil Supplies Department and the Kerala State 
Civil Supplies Corporation (Supplyco) to enhance the transparency and 
efficiency of the Public Distribution System (PDS). This software is 

65 
 
developed by C -Dac. The primary goal of VTFMS is to prevent the 
diversion of food grains and other essential commodities meant for the 
Public Distribution System. Previously, there were concerns about vehicles 
transporting these items to ration shops diverting them to private godowns 
or other illegal markets. VTFMS addresses this problem head -on by 
providing real-time tracking of every vehicle in the PDS supply chain. 
 
• Public Grievance Portal (PG Portal):  The portal provides a user -friendly 
interface for citizens to register their complaints or grievances related to the 
PDS. This includes issues concerning ration shops, food grain quality, non -
availability of stock, or any other service -related problems. The portal acts 
as a centralized platform where all complaints are registered. It 
automatically routes the complaints to the concerned officials based on the 
category and location of the grievance. 
 
• Aadhaar-enabled Public Distribution System (AePDS):  This system 
uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication and electronic Point of Sale 
(ePoS) devices at Fair Price Shops (FPSs). This ensures that beneficiaries 
are identified biometrically, preventing the use of bogus cards and the 
diversion of food grains. It also empowers citizens by allowing them to 
transact with any ePoS -enabled FPS in the country through the "One 
Nation, One Ration Card" (ONORC) scheme.”

68 
 
 
7.33 The Committee note from the case studies of Bihar, Meghalaya, 
Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Kerala that substantial progress has been made by 
States in digitization, Aadhaar seeding, ePoS deployment, online monitoring 
and SMART -PDS adoption; however, the pace and depth of implementation 
remain uneven. The Committee further note that Bihar has achieved 100 per 
cent digitization with over 98 per cent Aadhaar seeding and about 80 per cent 
e-KYC, Meghalaya had only 73 per cent Aadhaar seeding as on 30th April 2025, 
Telangana had 80 FPSs operating in offline mode, Tamil Nadu had 403 FPSs in 
no-network regions and Kerala itself has emphasized the need for a single 
Enterprise Resource Planning ( ERP)-based solution. The Committee , 
therefore, recommend that the Department should institutionalize a structured 
cross-learning framework under SMART -PDS so that best practices, workable 
solutions and operational innovations emerging from better -performing States 
are quickly replicated in lagging States through technical support, training, 
standard operating procedures and focused follow-up. 
(Recommendation No. 13) 
 
 
7.34 The Committee observe that State case studies reveal recurring 
operational constraints such as biometric authentication failures among 
elderly persons and manual labourers, poor network connectivity, incomplete 
module customization, pending grievance redressal and uneven acceptance of 
route optimisation under Anna Chakra. The y further note that acceptance of 
optimised routes was almost 100 per cent in Bihar, 70.64 per cent in 
Meghalaya, 97 per cent in Telangana, 20 per cent in Tamil Nadu and nil in 
Kerala, despite visible reductions in route distances and expected savings. 
The Committee are of the view that the Department should require each 
State/UT to prepare a time -bound reform agenda addressing authentication 
failures, connectivity gaps, module completion, grievance pendency and route 
optimisation, with quarterly review at the Central level so that the benefits of 
modernization are realized uniformly across the country rather than remaining 
confined to a few better-performing States. 
(Recommendation No. 14)

1.4 The Committee trust that utmost importance will be given to the implementation 
ofthe Observations / Recommendations accepted by the Government. The Committee 
desirethat Action Taken Notes in respect of Observations/Recommendations 
contained inChapter -I of this Report should be furnished to them at the earliest but

1.5 The Committee will now deal with some of t heir earlier 
Observations/Recommendationswhich either require reiteration or merit furthercomments. 
 
Recommendation No. 1 (Para No. 2.27) 
A. Scheme-wise Prioritisation of Resources in Demands for Grants 
1.6 The Committee had recommended as under: 
“The Committee note that the Budget Estimate of the Department of Consumer 
Affairs for 2026–27 is ₹4,497.37 crore. Out of this, ₹4,100 crore, which is about 91 
percent of the total allocation, has been provided for the Price Stabilisation Fund 
(PSF). The Depart ment has informed that although the PSF accounts for the 
largest share of the budget, the allocation for other schemes in 2026 –27 is higher 
than the previous year by about 5.22 percent and is considered adequate for 
consumer grievance redressal, enforcemen t activities and awareness 
programmes. 
The Committee recognise the importance of the PSF in stabilising prices of 
essential commodities. At the same time, they observe that such a large 
concentration of resources under a single scheme leaves relatively lim ited fiscal 
space for strengthening the institutional framework for consumer protection, 
including grievance redressal mechanisms, enforcement of standards and 
consumer awareness. 
The Committee recommend that the Department present a clearer scheme -wise 
prioritisation of resources in future Demands for Grants so that price stabilisation 
measures and institutional consumer protection systems develop in a balanced 
manner.” 
1.7 In its action-taken reply, the Ministry has stated as under: 
“Adequate provision ha s been kept keeping in view the anticipated requirements and 
estimated expenditure. In so far as the “SCC” Scheme is concerned, financial 
assistance is released to States/UTs based on eligible proposals received in 
accordance with the scheme guidelines and , therefore, the Budget Estimates (BE) 
and Revised Estimates (RE) are calibrated in view of the anticipated proposals and 
implementation requirements during a given financial year. Since inception, the SCC 
Scheme has enabled provision of financial assistan ce across States/UTs for 
strengthening the infrastructure of Consumer Commissions, thereby supplementing 

3 
 
the responsibility of State Governments in ensuring minimum infrastructural facilities 
for effective functioning of Consumer Commissions. During recent  years also, 
financial assistance has continued to be extended for physical and non -physical 
infrastructure subject to receipt of eligible proposals from States/UTs. 
        Further, “Consumer Protection Activities” focus on strengthening stakeholder 
engagement, awareness and institutional coordination for effective implementation of 
the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 through organisation of workshops/conferences, 
consultations, observance of National Consumer Day and World Consumer Rights 
Day and other rela ted activities. The expenditure under this component is also 
planned keeping in view the approved activities and estimated requirement during the 
financial year. 
 The CONFONET scheme is implemented through NIC, which raises fund 
demands for software upgrad ation, hardware support, cloud services, contractual 
manpower. Key activities include e -Jagriti platform, technical support to consumer 
commissions at National, State and District levels.  
 The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) receives funding from Govt of  India for 
the implementation of specific scheme, namely 'Setting up of Assaying and 
Hallmarking Centres'. Additionally, Quality Control Orders are issued by the 
concerned line Ministries/Departments, while the enforcement of standards is carried 
out by BIS using its own internal funds. 
 The Department has been generating consumer awareness through various 
media including electronic, digital and outdoor media, the focus for publicizing the 
consumer awareness initiatives has been through social media at zero  cost 
dissemination. There has been exponential growth in the number of followers of social 
media handles with increased engagement and reach. We have been able to garner 
attention as well as generate public engagement using social media platforms like X, 
Instagram, Facebook, Linked In, Telegram, Arattai, and Whatsapp in which we are 
having direct communication also with consumers. Other than social media, the 
Department has been interacting with Panchayats of States/UTs through virtual 
interactions to reac h the grassroot levels. Videos are being forwarded to States/ 
UTs/VCOs so that they may utilize those videos for generating awareness. The 
Department has been participating in fairs and festivals where large number of people 
from rural and backwards areas may congregate.   In Publicity division, funds are also 
allocated to NER, SC, ST regions in which Department in past has done has done 
various campaigns and in future proposes community engagement with women 
SHGs, Anganwadi workers, PDS beneficiaries out o f allocated funds. However, as 
and when the need arises for any major awareness campaigns for which provision of 
funds is not there, proposal will be put up for seeking funds.” 
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (Department of 
Consumer Affairs) O.M. No. N-12/1/2026-P&C Section dated 25th June, 2026] 
 
 

4 
 
 
1.8 The Committee in their original report had observed that a large concentration of 
resources under a single scheme leaves relatively limited fiscal space for strengthening the 
institutional framework for consumer protection, and had accordingly recommended that the 
Department present a clearer scheme -wise prioritisation of resources in future Demands for 
Grants. 
 The Committee note the Department's reply does not amount to the c learer scheme-
wise prioritisation of resources in future Demands for Grants. However, it defends the 
existing 91-per-cent concentration under the PSF rather than indicating how a more balanced 
prioritisation between price stabilisation and institutional co nsumer protection would be 
reflected going forward. The Committee, therefore, reiterate their recommendation that the 
Department present, in future Demands for Grants, a clearer scheme -wise prioritisation of 
resources so that price stabilisation measures and institutional consumer protection systems 
develop in a balanced manner. 
 
Recommendation No. 8 (Para No. 3.96) 
B. Vacancies in Consumer Commissions 
1.9 The Committee had recommended as under: 
“The Committee note that as on 31 January 2026 there are 18 va cancies of 
Presidents and 79 vacancies of Members in State Commissions and 179 
vacancies of Presidents and 397 vacancies of Members in District Commissions. 
The Department has stated that appointments to these positions fall under the 
jurisdiction of the respective State Governments. 
The Committee observe that such a large number of vacancies can affect the 
efficiency of consumer dispute resolution and may contribute to delays in disposal 
of cases. 
The Committee recommend that the Department continue engagi ng with State 
Governments and Union Territory administrations to ensure that vacancies in 
consumer commissions are filled at the earliest so that timely redressal of 
consumer grievances, enhance awareness about consumer rights, and promote 
fair business practices.” 
1.10 In its action-taken reply, the Ministry has stated as under: 
“Under the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the responsibility for 
appointment of Presidents and Members in the State and District Consumer 
Commissions rests with the respective State Governments. The Act also mandates 
that the process of appointments be initiated at least six months prior to occurrence of 
vacancies and provides enabling provisions for alternate arrangements to ensure 
continuity of functioning in ca se of vacancies. The Department of Consumer Affairs 
continuously engages with State Governments to expedite the filling up of vacancies 
and improve the overall functioning of Consumer Commissions. In addition, the e -

5 
 
Jagriti platform, with features such as e-filing, virtual hearings etc. is expected to 
mitigate capacity constraints, improve efficiency and reduce pendency. Moreover, 
several Consumer Commissions have achieved disposal rates exceeding 100% in 
recent periods, indicating improved operational effectiveness.” 
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (Department of 
Consumer Affairs) O.M. No. N-12/1/2026-P&C Section dated 25th June, 2026] 
1.11 The Committee note that as on 31 January 2026 there were 18 vacancies of 
Presidents and 79 v acancies of Members in State Commissions, and as many as 179 
vacancies of Presidents and 397 vacancies of Members in District Commissions. The 
Committee, while noting that such a large number of vacancies can affect the 
efficiency of consumer dispute resol ution and contribute to delays in disposal of 
cases, had recommended that the Department continue engaging with State 
Governments and Union Territory administrations to ensure that these vacancies are 
filled at the earliest. In response, the Department had  informed the Committee that 
appointments to these positions fall within the jurisdiction of the respective State 
Governments, and they are continuously engaging with State Governments to 
expedite the filling up of vacancies and improve the overall functio ning of Consumer 
Commissions.   
 The Committee note that the Department in its reply has reiterated the statutory  
position under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 that the Act mandates initiation of 
the appointment process at least six months prior to occu rrence of vacancies, and 
that enabling provisions exist for alternate arrangements pending such appointments. 
The Committee, however, observe that the reply does not indicate any specific, time -
bound steps, targets, or a mechanism for periodic review at an  appropriate level to fill 
the large number of vacancies. The Committee, therefore, reiterate their 
recommendation and urge the Department to pursue focused, time -bound 
engagement with State Governments and Union Territory administrations to expedite 
the filling of vacancies in State and District Consumer Commissions. 
Recommendation No. 11 (Para No.  3.99) 
C. Internationally Recognised Accreditation for the National Test House 
 1.12 The Committee had recommended as under: 
 “The Committee note that against the projected demand of ₹88.80 crore for the 
National Test House (NTH) during 2026–27, an allocation of ₹67.00 crore has been provided 
in the Budget Estimate. The Department has stated that the allocation, though lower than the 
projected demand, has been a ssessed as adequate to meet priority requirements and that 
ongoing projects, implementation capacity, statutory functions, infrastructure works, 
procurement of equipment and capacity-building activities will continue without disruption. 
 The Committee beli eve that the National Test House plays a critical role in 
strengthening the country’s quality infrastructure by providing testing and certification 
facilities across a wide range of industrial sectors. In view of the growing demand for reliable 

6 
 
testing fac ilities in emerging areas such as electric mobility, renewable energy equipment, 
electronics and advanced manufacturing, the need for strengthening and expanding testing 
infrastructure is expected to increase significantly. 
 The Committee, therefore, recom mend the Department to closely monitor the 
implementation of infrastructure expansion and laboratory modernisation projects under the 
National Test House to ensure that planned capacity augmentation is not delayed due to 
resource constraints. The Committee  also urge the Department to explore avenues for 
phased expansion of NTH facilities in emerging sectors and industrial clusters in each State 
so as to further strengthen the national quality infrastructure and effectively support industry 
in meeting evolving quality and safety standards. The Committee further recommend that the 
National Test House should pursue internationally recognised accreditations and strengthen 
alignment with global testing and certification frameworks so as to enhance international 
acceptance of its test results and support Indian industry in accessing global markets.”

 “The recommendations of the Hon'ble Committee have been noted and are being

 The Committee note that the Department has introduced certain reforms to improve

 The PSF market interventions are broadly based on buffer stocking for subsequent

 Integration of PSF with P rice Support Scheme (PSS) of Department of Agriculture &

acceptance of its test results and support Indian industry in accessing global markets. 
 
Reply of the Government 
 The recommendations of the Hon'ble Committee have been noted and are being 
addressed through ongoing infrastructure expansion, laboratory modernization, and capacity 
augmentation initiatives of NTH. 
NTH has established a robust monitoring mechanism for infrastructure expansion and 
laboratory modernization projects. A dedicated dashboard is being utilized to monitor project 
progress, and regular review meetings are conducted to assess impleme ntation status, 
identify bottlenecks, and ensure timely completion of activities. This mechanism facilitates 
effective monitoring of project execution, timely utilization of resources, and implementation 
of planned capacity augmentation initiatives. 
            Budget utilization is being monitored on a continuous basis to ensure that priority 
activities, including infrastructure development, laboratory modernization, procurement of 
testing equipment, and capacity -building initiatives, are undertaken in a timely manner. In 
case additional requirements arise on account of project expansion, capacity augmentation, 
or emerging sectoral needs, suitable proposals will be considered at the Revised Estimates 
stage, subject to availability of resources and approval of the competent authority. 
     NTH recognizes the growing demand for testing and certification services in emerging 
sectors such as electric mobility, renewable energy, electronics, and advanced 
manufacturing. In this regard, NTH is undertaking cap acity augmentation through the 

20 
 
establishment of new testing facilities and modernization of existing laboratories. The 
ongoing initiatives include the establishment of a Solar PV Module Testing Facility at 
Ghaziabad, a Solar Water Heater Testing Facility a t Chennai, an Integrated Test Facility for 
the Power Transmission and Distribution Sector at Jaipur, EV Battery Testing Facilities at 
Mumbai, Kolkata and Bengaluru, and a Drone Testing Facility at Ghaziabad. 
  Existing laboratories are also being upgraded with advanced testing infrastructure to 
meet emerging industrial and technological requirements. Through its network of 
laboratories, including NABL -accredited laboratories, NTH provides testing and quality 
assurance services to industry, government depart ments, regulatory authorities, public 
sector undertakings, and other stakeholders across the country. The impact of these 
initiatives is reflected in improved operational performance. During FY 2025 –26, the number 
of samples tested increased by 10.57%, fro m 45,959 to 50,815, while revenue generation 
increased by 20.09%, from ₹44.45 crore to ₹53.38 crore, as compared to FY 2024 –25. NTH 
has also reduced the turnaround time for testing of samples through process optimization 
and improved utilization of testing  infrastructure, enabling faster delivery of testing and 
quality assurance services and strengthening domestic testing capabilities. 
        NTH continues to maintain and expand nationally recognized accreditations and align 
its testing and certification p ractices with internationally accepted standards and conformity 
assessment frameworks. Efforts are being made to strengthen quality systems, enhance 
technical competence, and expand the scope of accredited services so as to improve 
international acceptance of NTH test reports and facilitate access of Indian industry to global 
markets. 
            NTH will continue to take necessary measures to strengthen its infrastructure, testing 
capabilities, and service delivery in line with evolving industry requiremen ts and national 
priorities. 
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (Department of 
Consumer Affairs) O.M. No. N-12/1/2026-P&C Section dated 25th June, 2026] 
Comments of the Committee 
(Please see Para No. 1.14 of Chapter I of the Report) 
 
Recommendation No. 12 (Para No.  3.100) 
 
 The Committee note that the Budget Estimates under the Consumer Awareness 
Scheme have remained almost stagnant at around ₹19 crore since 2023 –24, despite higher 
Revised Estimates and actual expenditure in certain y ears. While the Committee appreciate 
the Department’s efforts to utilise social media and other low -cost digital platforms for wider 
dissemination of consumer awareness messages, they are of the view that digital outreach 
alone may not be sufficient, particularly in rural and backward areas. 
 The Committee, therefore, recommend the Department to review the adequacy of the 
present allocation and consider enhancing it in future, while adopting a balanced approach 

21 
 
combining digital campaigns with on -ground awareness activities through States/UTs, local 
institutions and public representatives to ensure wider and more effective outreach. The 
Committee also desire the Department to emphasise on the potential of social media 
outreach which needs to be further expan ded and strategically utilised to reach a wider and 
younger audience. 
  
Reply of the Government 
 Given the increased digitalization in the country, the Department has been utilizing 
social media at zero dissemination cost to generate awareness. There has been exponential 
growth in the number of followers of social media handles with increased engagement and 
reach. Other than social media, the Department has been interacting with Panchayats of 
States/UTs through virtual interactions to reach the grassroot l evels. Videos are being 
forwarded to States/ UTs/VCOs so that they may utilize those videos for generating 
awareness. The Department has been participating in fairs and festivals where large number 
of people from rural and backwards areas may congregate. F urther, traditional media like 
SMS, IVRS are being used for rural and backward areas.  In Publicity division, funds are also 
allocated to NER, SC, ST regions in which Department in past has done various campaigns 
 and in future proposes community engagemen t with women SHGs, Anganwadi workers, 
PDS beneficiaries out of allocated funds. However, as and when the need arises for any 
major awareness campaigns for which provision of funds is not there, proposal will be put up 
for seeking funds. The level of awaren ess can be judged from the fact that the number of 
complaints registered at NCH has increased through the succeeding years. 
 
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (Department of 
Consumer Affairs) O.M. No. N-12/1/2026-P&C Section dated 25th June, 2026]

A. Scheme for Modernization and Reforms through Technology in 
Public Distribution System (SMART-PDS) 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 5, Para No. 3.40) 
 
1.5  The Committee in their original report observed/recommended as follows:- 
 
“The Committee note that the during 2025 -26, the actual utilization of the 
funds under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Modernization and 
Reforms through Technology in Public Distribution System (SMART -
PDS) has been at     Rs. 23.18 crore against Rs 51.00 crore at RE 2025 -
26. The reason for decrease in budget allocation during 2025 -26 at RE 
stage, the Department informed that Scheme for Modernization and 
Reforms through Technology in Public Distribution System (SMART -
PDS)” has to be onboarded on SNA SPARSH platform w.e.f. 01.07.2025. 
Due to delay in onboarding and in submission of financial proposal by 
States/UTs, funds could not be released. The Committee understand that 
the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Modernization and Reforms through 
Technology in Public Distribution System (SMART -PDS) has been 
introduced to strengthen transparency, efficiency and accountability in the 
Public Distribution System through technology -driven reforms. The 
extension of the scheme for the period 2026 –2031 under the umbrella 
programme Scheme for Assistance in Ration Transport and Handling -
Income with Automation in PDS (SARTHAK -PDS) to strengthen backend 
interoperability, enhance data analytics, upgrade infrastructure and 
improve grievance redressal mechanisms is under consideration. 
 
The Committee emphasize that SMART -PDS is an important 
initiative aimed at strengthening transparency, efficiency and 
accountability in the Public Distribution System through technology -driven 
reforms. The Committee, therefore, recommend the Department to 
expedite the full -scale implementation of SMART -PDS across all States 
and Union Territories by strengthening coordination with State 

3 
 
Governments, ensuring timely onboarding on digital financial platforms, 
and simplifying procedures for submission of financial proposals and 
release of funds. The Committee further note that the extension of the 
scheme for the period 2026 –2031 under the umbrella programme 
SARTHAK-PDS is under consideration and urge the Government to 
expedite its finalization while incorporating measures to enhance backend 
interoperability, data analytics, infrastructure upgradation and grievance 
redressal mechanisms to ensure more efficient delivery of PDS services.” 
 
1.6  The Ministry in its action taken reply has stated as under:- 
 
“The Department of Food and Public Distribution acknowledges the 
observations and recommendations of the Hon’ble Standing Committee 
regarding expediting the full -scale implementation of the Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme “SMART-PDS”. 
 
The development and implementation of the SMART -PDS platform 
has been entrusted to the National Informatics Centre (NIC), which has 
made significant progress in developing all core modules of the system 
within the prescribed timelines. These modules include Ration Card 
Management System (RCMS), Supply Chain Management and 
Allocation, Distribution and Procurement. 
 
As per the current status of implementation, the RCMS module has 
been deployed in 16 States/UTs, while the Supply Chain and Allocation 
module, as well as Distribution module, have been implemented across 
22 and 30 States/UTs respectively. 
 
It is submitted that while the core application has been developed 
centrally, the implementation across States/UTs requires State -specific 
configuration, data migration, customization and integration with existing 
systems, which has a bearing on the pace of rollout. The Department has 
been actively coordinating with States/UTs and NIC to ensure timely 
onboarding, including facilitation of financial approvals, handholding 
support and regular review meetings. 
 
Further, with respect to the observations regarding delays in fund 
utilization, it is submitted that onboarding on SNA SPARSH platform and 
submission of financial proposals by States/UTs are key prerequisites for 
fund release. The Department has taken necessary steps to streamline 
these processes and is continuously engaging with States/UTs to 
expedite compliance. 
 
The Department is committed to ensuring full -scale implementation 
of SMART - PDS across all States/UTs in a time -bound manner, in line 
with the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
Further, the extension of the SMART -PDS scheme for the period 
2026–2031 under the umbrella SARTHAK -PDS scheme has been 
approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA). The 

4 
 
scheme aims to further strengthen backend interoperability, enhance data 
analytics capabilities, upgrade infrastructure and improve grievance 
redressal mechanisms, thereby ensuring more efficient and transparent 
delivery of PDS services.” 
 
 
1.7 The Committee note from the action taken reply that the core 
modules of SMART-PDS, namely Ration Card Management System (RCMS), 
Supply Chain Management and Allocation, Distribution and Procurement 
have been developed by NIC and implementation has progressed in 
different States/UTs. The Committee also note that extension of SMART -
PDS under the umbrella SARTHAK -PDS scheme for the period 2026 -2031 
has been approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.  
 
The Committee while reiterating their earlier recommendation  desire 
the Department to ensure that the remaining State -specific configuration, 
data migration, integration with existing systems, onboarding on SNA -
SPARSH platform and release of funds are completed in a time -bound 
manner. The Committee may be apprised about the State/UT-wise 
implementation status, funds released/utilised and timelines for full rollout  
of SMART-PDS across the Country. 
 
 
B. Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No.  6, Para No. 3.49) 
 
1.8 The Committee in their original report observed/recommended as follows:- 
 
“The Committee note that the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana 
(PMGKAY) has emerged as a major food security intervention for the 
poor and vulnerable sections of the country by providing free foodgrains 
to beneficiaries covered under the National Food Security Act, 2013 
(NFSA). The Committee also take note that the scheme involves a 
substantial financial commitment, with ₹2,05,250 crore allocated in BE 
2024–25, ₹2,03,000 crore in BE 2025 –26 and ₹2,27,429 crore in BE 
2026–27, reflecting the Government’s continued emphasis on food 
security. The Committee observe that the scheme currently covers about 
80.56 crore beneficiaries against the intended coverage of 81.35 crore 
persons, indicating that around 0.79 crore eligible persons are still yet to 
be identified and included under the scheme. The Committee are of the 
view that the continued reliance on 2011 Census data for determining 

5 
 
NFSA coverage may lead to exclusion of newly eligible and vulnerable 
households due to population growth, migration and socio -economic 
changes. The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Government, in 
coordination with the State/UT Governments, undertake a comprehensive 
and time -bound exercise to update the beneficiary database, intensify 
identification of the remaining 0.79 crore eligible persons and periodically 
revise the coverage limits in line with updated population estimates.” 
 
1.9 The Ministry in its action taken reply has stated as under:- 
 
“The Central Government has issued advisories to all the States/Union 
Territories from time to time to identify all eligible and poor persons/ 
households including vulnerable Sections of the Society for inclusion 
under the NFSA. States undertake updation of their beneficiary database 
so that ineligible ration cards get deleted and better targeting of rightful 
beneficiaries is ensured. Thus, deletion of ineligible beneficiaries and 
addition of eligible beneficiaries under the Act is a continuous process.” 
 
1.10 The Committee had recommended a comprehensive and time -bound 
exercise to update the beneficiary database, intensify identification of the 
remaining 0.79 crore eligible persons and periodically revise the coverage 
limits in line with updated population estimates. The reply of the 
Department is general in nature and merely states that advisories have 
been issued and addition/deletion of beneficiaries is a continuous process. 
The reply does not indicate any time -bound exercise, State/UT -wise 
roadmap or any proposal for revision of coverage limits in line with updated 
population estimates. The Committee, therefore, reiterate their original 
recommendation and desire the Department to undertake a comprehensive, 
time-bound and verifiable exercise in coordination with States/UTs and 
apprise the Committee of concrete steps taken in this regard. 
 
C.  Dues and Liabilities of Food Corporation of India (FCI) 
Recommendation (Sl. No.  7, Para No. 3.53)   
1.11 The Committee in their original report observed/recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee observe that FCI supplies foodgrains to various 
Ministries/Departments for implementation of welfare schemes, including 
the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) and the Mid -Day Meal 
Scheme, on a payment basis and that delays in reimbursement by the 
concerned Ministries lead to accumulation of outstanding dues for FCI. The 
Committee note that in the case of the Ministry of Human Resource 
Development (now the Ministry of Education), outstanding dues under the 

6 
 
Mid-Day Meal Scheme persist ₹205.93 crore as on 31.12.2025 
(provisional) despite periodic payments.  
 
The Committee recommend that the Department should evolve a time -
bound payment framework for all Ministries and Departments receiving 
foodgrains from FCI under welfare schemes, including mandatory timelines 
for reimbursement and periodic reconciliation of accounts. The Committee 
emphasize the importance of pursuing this matter at the highest levels, 
engaging with the concerned Ministry directly to resolve the matter in time 
bound manner.” 
 
1.12  The Ministry in its action taken reply has stated as under:- 
 
 “As per Gol guidelines, after the issue of food grains under the MDM 
Scheme, the FCI raises monthly bills on the Revenue District 
Administration/MDM Office within 10 days of the following month after the 
lifting of stocks. The District Administration is required to make payment 
within 20 days of receipt of the bill from FCI.” 
 
1.13     The Committee had recommended evolution of a time -bound 
payment framework for all Ministries/Departments receiving foodgrains 
from FCI under welfare schemes, including mandatory timelines for 
reimbursement and periodic reconciliation of accounts. The Department, in 
its reply, has only referred to the existing guidelines regarding raising of 
monthly bills and payment within 20 days by the District Administration. 
The reply does not specify the reason for  the outstanding dues of              
Rs. 205.93 crore under the Mid -Day Meal Scheme as on 31.12.2025 
(provisional), nor does it indicate any higher -level institutional mechanism 
for reconciliation and liquidation of pending dues. The Committee, 
therefore, reiterate their recommendation and desire the Department to 
evolve a robust inter -Ministerial payment and reconciliation framework and 
furnish the status of outstanding dues and prompt action to clear the same.

Recommendation (Sl. No.1, Para No. 2.19) 
 
      The Committee note that total Budget allocated to the Department of 
Food & Public Distribution is Rs. 285047.20 crore for the year 2026 -27 which 
includes Rs. 235024.58 crore for Revenue section and Rs. 50022.62 crore under

Reply of the Government 
 
2.16 STORAGE OF FOODGRAINS AND AUGMENTATION OF 
STORAGE CAPACITY:      
FCI continuously assesses and monitors the storage capacity and based 
on the storage gap assessment, storage capacities are created/hired. The 
requirement of Storage capacity in FCI depends upon the level of procurement, 
requirement of buffer norms and PDS operations for Rice and Wheat 
mainly.  Storage gap is assessed in the procuring States based on the highest 
stock levels in the last three years and in the consuming States on the basis of 
4 months (6 months in case of NE regions) requirement of National Food 
Security Act (NFSA) and Other Welfare Scheme (OWS) for creation / 
construction of new godowns.  
The land acquisition for own godown is tedious task. Further, 
augmentation of storage capacity involving private entrepreneurs not only 
expedite the construction process but also reduce long term liability as the 
option to de-hire the surplus capacity in lean period exist. 
FCI hires storage capacities from CWC/ SWC/ State Agencies/ Private 
Agencies wherever required while ensuring optimum utilization of existing 
capacities. As on 01.03.2026, the Storage capacity of 483.70 LMT is available 
with Food Corporation of India and 463.40 LMT is available with State 
agencies for Central Pool stock of Foodgrains. As a result, a total covered 
capacity 947.10 LMT is available for storage of Central Pool stock of 
Foodgrains.  
 Further, FCI is augmenting its storage capacity through following schemes:   
a. Private Entrepreneurs Guarantee (PEG) Scheme 
b. Private Warehousing Scheme (PWS) 
c. Creation of godown under Asset Monetization 
d. Hiring of godown from CWC/ SWCs/ State Agencies 
e. Centre Sector Scheme (CSS)[Culminated on 31.03.2025] 
f. Construction of SILO's under PPP mode 
 Private Entrepreneurs Guarantee (PEG) Scheme 
i. Private Entrepreneurs Guarantee (PEG) Scheme-2008/09:         
       To address Storage needs due to increasing procurement, a scheme to 
create godowns was initiated in 2008. The godowns under this scheme are 
constructed by mobilizing private investment. FCI gives 10 years guarantee on 
the godowns constructed under this Scheme at identified locations to private 
parties and 9 years for CWC & SWC. The first offer is given to CWC/SWC for 
creation of required capacity on their own land. In this case, Govt. approved 
rent is paid for 9 years guarantee period. In case of private investors, the 
tenders and rates are decided by process of competitive bidding through e -

19 
 
tenders. The guarantee given in this case is for 10 years. The investor has to 
quote rate in Rs per quintal per month, the successful bidder has to arrange 
land and create godowns as per FCI specification at his own cost. 
Subsequently, guarantee is released by FCI after inspection. 
  On 28.7.2008 the Government of India had circulated the PEG scheme - 
2008 to FCI and State Govts. (Non DCP States) vide which Assessment of the 
storage need was made by FCI based on the overall procurement/consumption 
needs of the area and existing storage capacity. In Consuming States, 
assessment was based on 4 months' requirements of stocks for NFSA & OWS 
and in Procuring States assessment was based on highest stock level in the 
last three years. 
    On demand of DCP States, Govt. of India circulated PEG scheme - 2009 on 
08-04-2010. As per Scheme, SLC is headed by the Secretary (Food) of the 
State and the assessment of required storage capacity. The locally procured 
stock are envisaged to be kept equivalent to 14 months’ offtake under NFSA/ 
OWS Scheme. So, if the procurement is more than 14 months’ offtake, the 
capacity equivalent to 14 months is considered adequate. If the procurement is 
less than 14 months’ of offtake but more than 4 months’ offtake, capacity 
equivalent to procurement level is envisaged to be created. However, in any 
case the capacity equivalent to 4 months’ offtake under NFSA/ OWS scheme 
is required in the DCP States too. 
    Total capacity sanctioned for godowns as on 01.03.2026 is 150.97 LMT. Out 
of this, 148.61 LMT has been completed.

Total capacity hired under PWS is 30.87 LMT as on 01.01.2026.  
c. Creation of godown under Asset Monetization 
  Total 177 locations (17.34 LMT) under Cat. A assets were identified in FCI 
for construction of godowns under the Asset Monetization Scheme at FCI own 
land. Out of this tenders for 91 locations (9.33 LMT) have been floated and 
58,950 MT capacity has already been taken over. The remaining capacity is at 
various stages of construction/tendering.  
d. Hiring of godown from CWC/ SWCs/State Agencies 
  FCI also hires godown from CWC/ SWCs on guaranteed reservation basis 
to meet the requirement of storage space. As on 01.03.2026, a capacity of 
39.90 LMT hired from CWC and 121.73 LMT capacity from SWCs & 19.49 
LMT hired from State Govt.  
e. Centre Sector Scheme (CSS) 
  Government of India has implemented Central Sector Scheme (2017 -25) 
for the construction of godowns with a focus on augmenting storage capacity in 
the States of the North-Eastern (NE) Region and a few other states. Under this 
Scheme, a total capacity of 1,05,890 MT in NE regions and 54,760 in Other 
than NE regions was approved to be completed with a financial outlay of        
Rs. 484.08 Cr (Rs. 379.50 Cr for NE & Rs. 104.58 Cr for Other than NE).  
Till date, a total capacity of 1,23,970 MT (72,550 MT in NE regions and 
51,420 MT in Other than NE regions) has already been created by FCI under 
this Scheme. Further, capacity of 33,340 MT (02 in NE with 30,000 MT 
capacity and 01 in Himachal Pradesh with 3340 MT capacity) shall be added to 
above with completion of the last 3 Works under the Scheme in 2026-27.  
The directions of the Committee on exploring innovative and cost -effective 
storage solutions such as mobile storage units in geographically challenging 
regions have been duly noted and it is submitted that it is already a continuous 
process at FCI where advanced technologies being used globally are explored 
and studied for their suitability for implementation as per FCI's requirements. 
This scheme has been culminated on 31st March 2025. 
  
 
 

21 
 
f. Construction of SILOs under PPP mode 
 In order to upgrade and modernize the storage facilities, Silos across the 
Country under PPP mode are constructed as per approval of GoI, on the basis 
of State wise/revenue district wise storage gap assessment. 
  Accordingly, Silos at 57 locations with capacity 32.25 LMT have been 
completed and Silos at 78 locations with capacity 32.375 LMT are under 
construction.  
Further, in Phase -2 of the Hub & Spoke model, work awarded for 25.125 
LMT silos at 54 locations in 17 bundles/Projects under DBFOO mode. 
 
 Innovative and cost effective storage solutions 
 In an effort to explore innovative solutions for foodgrain storage following 
options are being explored:  
i. Hermetic Storage:  Possibility of Hermetic Storage of foodgrain is being 
explored. CWC and FCI together are exploring this option.  
ii. Mechanized Godown:  FCI has taken initiative in direction of fully 
mechanized godown. A pilot project at two locations i.e. Whitefield, 
Bengaluru and Avadi, Chennai has been started on FCI own land. Bids 
received are under process of finalization. 
iii. Smart Warehouse:   FCI has started the process of upgrading its own 
godown as smart warehouses. Wherein some critical parameters like 
temperature, humidity and phosphine gas, fire hazards, humidity, 
unauthorized entry etc. are mentioned on real time basis. Automatic 
number plate reader (ANPR) will be placed at depot gate. The provision of 
AI Based bag counting mechanism through sensors is also planned.  
iv. CCTV: Real time monitoring of FCI depots is being ensured through a 
Command & Control Centre established at FCI Hqrs. AI -Based, Fish-eye 
Cameras & Bullet cameras are being installed in all FCI depots to monitor 
stocks and depot operations. 
v. VLTS: Vehicle Location Tracking System has been implemented for road 
transportation of foodgrains. 
 
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public 
Distribution (Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
O.M. No. G-20017/03/2023-AC Dated 15th June, 2026] 
 
 
 

22 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 9, Para No. 4.17) 
 
2.17   The Committee note that steel silos provide a highly automated and 
scientific method of storing foodgrains in a monitored atmosphere, enabling 
bulk handling through mechanized loading and unloading systems. The 
Committee further note that silo-based storage requires only about one -third of 
the land area compared to conventional storage facilities and facilitates 
efficient bulk movement of foodgrains through railway siding infrastructure, 
thereby reducing handling time and transportation costs. The Committee 
recommend that the pace of expansion of silo capacity needs to be further 
accelerated in order to gradually reduce dependence on conventional storage 
methods and minimize post -harvest losses. The Committee opined that the 
Department should prepare a comprehensive and time -bound roadmap for 
expanding modern silo storage infrastructure across major procuring and 
consuming States, with special emphasis on integrating silo facilities with 
railway networks and containerized bulk movement systems.   
The Committee also recommend that pilot projects for rice storage in silos 
be expeditiously implemented and evaluated so that the benefits of modern 
storage technology can be extended beyond wheat to other foodgrains.  
 
Reply of the Government 
 
2.18 In order to upgrade and modernize the storage facilities, 
Government of India has approved construction of Silos across the Country 
under PPP mode. 
 
 Accordingly, Silos at 57 locations with capacity 32.25 LMT have been 
completed and Silos at 78 locations with capacity 32.375 LMT are under 
construction.  
  
Further, in Phase -2 of the Hub & Spoke model, FCI awarded tenders for 
25.125 LMT silos at 54 locations in 17 bundles/Projects under DBFOO mode. 
  
Regarding Rice silo, 0.125 LMT silo each at Kaimur & Buxar has been 
operationalised for Rice storage and both varieties of Rice i.e . Par Boiled & 
Raw Rice. 
  
Since this is a pilot Rice silo project, the quality of Rice stored in the silos is 
being assessed in consultation with independent experts, as well as the QC 
and Engineering Divisions of FCI. Upon completion of this assessment, the 
necessary technical and structural modifications will be finalized and 
incorporated into future silo tenders.  
 
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public 
Distribution (Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
O.M. No. G-20017/03/2023-AC Dated 15th June, 2026] 

23 
 
 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 10, Para No. 5.18) 
 
2.19   The Committee note that the Department of Food and Public Distribution 
has undertaken several advanced technological interventions for modernizing 
the management of foodgrains and strengthening the Public Distribution 
System (PDS) through the introduction of digital platforms such as Enterprise 
Resource Planning (ERP) under SMART -PDS, the Anna Sahayata Holistic AI 
Solution (ASHA),   the Warehouse Inventory Network & Governing System 
(WINGS) and Scheme for Assistance in Ration Transport and Handling -
Income with Automation in PDS (SARTHAK PDS) which is an umbrella 
scheme integrating Assistance for intra -State movement & handling of 
foodgrains and FPS dealer margins (NFSA) and Technology -driven PDS 
reforms Strengthens implementation of NFSA, 2013. The Committee also note 
that total SMART PDS Outlay for 5 years is ₹829.88 Crore (proposed) out of 
which the Central Share is ₹ 753 crore and State Share is ₹76.80 crore. 
Budgetary allocation for Year 1 has been kept at ₹194 Cr (as per SARTHAK -
PDS first-year financial planning). Further, the consolidated budget for Module 
Development and Rollout of all the components of ASHA has been kept at 
Rs.120 cr for five years with Rs.30 allocation for year 1. 
   While appreciating the technology and AI driven interventions in the 
system, the Committee recommend that the Department of Food and Public 
Distribution ensure the time-bound and coordinated implementation of 
technological initiatives under SMART -PDS, including the deployment of ERP 
systems, the Anna Sahayata Holistic AI Solution (ASHA), and the Warehouse 
Inventory Network & Governing System (WINGS). The Department should also 
ensure effective operationalization of the Scheme for Assistance in Ration 
Transport and Handling – Income with Automation in PDS (SARTHAK PDS) so 
that the integration of intra -State movement and handling assistance, FPS 
dealer margins, and technology-driven reforms strengthens the implementation 
of the National Food Security Act, 2013. 
   
Reply of the Government 
 
2.20       The Department has undertaken significant steps to ensure 
systematic and phased implementation of SMART -PDS across all States/UTs. 
The development of the SMART-PDS platform, including its core ERP modules 
such as Ration Card Management System (RCMS), Supply Chain 
Management, Allocation, Distribution and Procurement has been entrusted to 
the National Informatics Centre (NIC), which has successfully developed these 
modules within stipulated timelines. 
  
The implementation of these modules is being carried out in close 
coordination with States/UTs, as it involves State -specific configuration, 
integration with existing legacy systems and data migration. Regular review 

24 
 
meetings, capacity -building initiatives and technical handholding are being 
undertaken to ensure adherence to timelines and smooth rollout. 
  
With respect to the Anna Sahayata Holistic AI Solution (ASHA), the 
Department has initiated large -scale deployment for AI -based citizen 
engagement and grievance redressal. The platform is being scaled up in a 
phased manner across States/UTs, with focus on multilingual interaction, real -
time feedback capture and integration with grievance redressal systems. 
  
Further, the Warehouse Inventory Network & Governing System (WINGS) 
and other supply chain digitization initiatives are being aligned with SMART -
PDS architecture to ensure end -to-end visibility and efficiency in foodgrain 
management. 
  
The Department has also formulated the SARTHAK -PDS scheme (2026 –
31) as an umbrella programme to integrate intra -State movement and handling 
assistance, FPS dealer margins and advanced technology -driven reforms. The 
SARTHAK-PDS scheme has been approved by the Cabinet Committee on 
Economic Affairs (CCEA) and envisages strengthening of backend 
interoperability, analytics, monitoring systems and service delivery 
mechanisms. 
  
The Department remains committed to ensuring time -bound 
implementation, effective coordination with States/UTs and seamless 
integration of technological interventions, so as to further strengthen 
transparency, efficiency and accountability in the Public Distribution System in 
alignment with the objectives of the National Food Security Act, 2013. 
  
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public 
Distribution (Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
O.M. No. G-20017/03/2023-AC Dated 15th June, 2026] 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 11, Para No. 5.19) 
 
2.21  The Committee appreciate the initiative taken by the Food Corporation of 
India through the development of the FCI Depot Darpan Portal as a digital 
mechanism for systematic monitoring and evaluation of depot infrastructure 
and operational efficiency. The portal, with its star -rating system, structured 
self-assessment framework, and multi -layered verification process, has the 
potential to significantly enhance transparency, accountability, and 
performance benchmarking across FCI-owned and hired depots. However, the 
Committee note that the portal presently does not include provisions for 
predictive analysis, which could further strengthen planning and preventive 
maintenance of storage infrastructure. The Committee, therefore, recommend 
that the Department further strengthen the Depot Darpan Portal by 
incorporating predictive analytics and data -driven decision support systems to 
identify infrastructure deficiencies and forecast maintenance requirements. The 
star-rating results generated through the portal should be directly linked with 
time-bound action plans for infrastructure upgradation and allocation of 

25 
 
maintenance funds so that depots graded below acceptable standards are 
improved expeditiously.  
 
Reply of the Government 
 
2.22 The Analytics part of Depot Darpan Portal is being handled with the 
Business Analytics tool which generates reports on operational efficiency 
parameters. The portal provides multiple reports for identification of 
deficiencies and performance gaps. 
  
Further, noncompliance with infrastructure grading parameters is linked 
with predefined triggers and timelines, ensuring time -bound action for 
infrastructure upgradation and maintenance of substandard depots. 
  
The Committee has rightly emphasized the need for integrating predictive 
analytics and data -driven decision support systems to improve planning, 
maintenance and monitoring of storage infrastructure. At present, the Depot 
Darpan Portal primarily functions as an assessment and monitoring tool; 
however, its upgradation into an AI -enabled platform would enable proactive 
identification of infrastructure deficiencies and facilitate timely interventions. 
   
In this regard, it is observed that implementation of AI -based features 
would require availability of standardized and reliable historical data, 
stabilization of the existing system and necessary technical support for 
development and integration of such modules. Further, appropriate safeguards 
would also be required to ensure transparency and reliability of AI -driven 
outputs. 
  
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public 
Distribution (Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
O.M. No. G-20017/03/2023-AC Dated 15th June, 2026] 
 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 12, Para No. 5.22) 
 
2.23  The Committee note that the Department of Food & Public 
Distribution (DFPD) has explored the use of Central Bank Digital Currency 
(CBDC) – Digital Food Coupons as a pilot initiative aiming to provide secure, 
programmable, purpose -bound digital tokens that can be redeemed only for 
foodgrains at authorized Fair Price Shops (FPSs) ensuring leakage reduction, 
real-time subsidy tracking and instant transfer of funds for PDS.  
The Committee understand that separate budgetary funds have not been 
allocated for the CBDC pilot project, as the Department intends to utilize the 
existing food subsidy outlay under PMGKAY for its implementation.  
The Committee are happy to note that the Department is taking proactive 
measures in bringing innovations in making the system easy for the 

26 
 
beneficiaries and recommend the Department to evaluate the outcome of the 
scheme and try to rollout CBDC -based digital food coupons in other parts of 
the country, and prepare a roadmap for nationwide implementation. Further, 
dedicated budgeting should be done to scale up the CBDC mechanism 
nationwide and to cover the costs of technological infrastructure, training, 
integration with FPSs, monitoring and grievance redressal etc. 
  
Reply of the Government 
 
 2.24 This Department has launched a pilot project on the use of Central 
Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) in the Public Distribution System (PDS) in the 
State of Gujarat on 15.02.2026. It has also launched a pilot project on use of 
CBDC for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under the Pradhan Mantri Garib 
Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) in Puducherry on 26.02.2026. The CBDC 
shall offer a secure, instant, traceable and programmable digital cash 
mechanism for PMGKAY beneficiaries, enabling smoother fund flow and 
reducing friction in availing entitlements. The benefits of use of CBDC, inter 
alia, include empowerment to beneficiaries availing entitled foodgrains; 
convenience of wallet-based payments reducing cash handling & leakage. 
 
            An Inter -Departmental Committee, three sub - Committees and one 
Technical Committee has been constituted for examination and formulation of 
roadmap for implementation and scaling up of Central Bank Digital Currency 
(CBDC) for delivery of food subsidy under the Public Distribution System 
(PDS) and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). 
 
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public 
Distribution (Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
O.M. No. G-20017/03/2023-AC Dated 15th June, 2026] 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 13, Para No. 6.26) 
 
2.25 The Committee note that the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) 
Programme is a key initiative of the Government to reduce crude oil import 
dependency, conserve foreign exchange, lower carbon emissions and provide 
additional income to sugarcane farmers. Under this programme, the 
Government has set a 20% ethanol blending target with petrol by Ethanol 
Supply Year (ESY) 2025 -26, requiring about 1,350 crore litres of ethanol, with 
a production capacity of 1,700 crore litres assuming 80% plant efficiency. The 
Committee commend the progress made under the Ethanol Blended Petrol 
(EBP) Programme, particularly the achievement of a 19.98% ethanol blending 
level as on 31.01.2026 against the targeted 20% blending by Ethanol Supply 
Year (ESY) 2025–26.  

27 
 
The Committee note that Budget Estimate for FY 2026 -27 under the 
scheme for extending financial assistance to sugar Mills for enhancement and 
augmentation of ethanol production capacity is Rs. 600 crore against the 
tentative demand of Rs. 1,000 crore from NABARD due to increased number 
of eligible sugar mills and distilleries. In this regard, the Committee, therefore, 
recommend the Department to provide adequate financial support for targeted 
policy interventions under the EBP programme which are critical to achieving 
energy security, environmental benefits, farmer welfare and a sustainable 
sugar-ethanol ecosystem. 
  
Reply of the Government 
 
2.26   Since, against the demand of Rs. 1000 crores in FY 2026 -27, only           
Rs. 600 crores have been approved at BE stage, therefore to provide adequate 
financial support for targeted policy interventions under the EBP programme, 
this Department would raise demand of additional funds (Supplementary 
Grant) of Rs. 400 crores at the RE stage for the FY 2026-27. 
  
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public 
Distribution (Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
O.M. No. G-20017/03/2023-AC Dated 15th June, 2026] 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 14, Para No. 7.16) 
 
2.27    The Committee note that domestic production of edible oils remains 
insufficient to meet national demand, resulting in heavy reliance on imports of 
Crude Palm Oil, Refined Palm Oil, Crude Soybean Oil and Crude Sunflower Oil 
which accounted for 56–57% of total availability in recent years (2019-20 to 2023-
24). The gap between demand and supply of edible oils is met through imports. 
On the matter of controlling continuous rise in edible oil prices over the past year, 
they have been apprised that Central Government had reduced the Basic 
Customs Duty on crude edible oils (crude soybean oil, crude palm oil and crude 
sunflower oil) from 20% to 10% with effect from 30th May 2025. While 
acknowledging this step, the Committee are of the view that the continued 
demand–supply gap and price volatility in cooking oils require sustained policy 
attention.  
  The Committee, therefore recommend the Department to adopt a 
coordinated approach for enhancing domestic production of oilseeds, implement 
prudent import -export policies and strengthening market stabilization 
mechanisms. Such measures would help reduce import dependence, achieve 
self-reliance in edible oils, protect consumer interests and ensure remunerative 
returns for farmers. 
 

28 
 
Reply of the Government 
 
2.28 The management of edible oils in the country is undertaken through a 
coordinated, multi -pronged strategy. This includes continuous assessment of 
domestic demand and availability from indigenous sources, with any demand -
supply gap addressed through calibrated imports to maintain price stability. This 
Department also closely monitors domestic and international price trends and 
recommends appropriate policy interventions as required. 
In line with the Committee's recommendations, the Department will 
continue to strengthen efforts towards enhancing domestic oilseed production, 
adopting prudent trade policies, and reinforcing market stabilisation mechanisms 
to reduce import dependence, safeguard consumer interests and ensure 
remunerative returns to farmers.  
[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public 
Distribution (Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
O.M. No. G-20017/03/2023-AC Dated 15th June, 2026]

REPORT 
CHAPTER – I 
 
This Report of the Standing Committee on Consumer Affairs, Food and 
Public Distribution deals with the action taken by the Government on the 
Observations/Recommendations contained in the Thirty Eighth Report of the 
Committee (Seventeenth Lok Sabha) on the subject ‘Functioning of Warehousing 
Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA)’ pertaining to the Ministry of

outreach of the same may be expanded.

Recommendation (Sl. No. 6) 
 
1.6  The Committee had recommended as under: 
 
The Committee note that there has been a shift towards the adoption of  digital 
solutions and technology for the process of verification, inspection and monitoring of 
weighing and measuring instruments. The Committee desire that a system should be 
constructed wherein all fuel dispensed should be monitored and any irregulariti es in the 
process be reported instantly to the concerned agencies. As Central Consumer Protection 
Authority (CCPA) is authorized to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers 
and unfair trade practices, the Committee, therefore, recommen d that in the event of such 
irregularity in the fuel station, an instant alert should go to the agency, i.e. the CCPA for its 
necessary action. 
  
1.7    In its action-taken reply, the Ministry has stated as under: 
 
“The Government emphasizes its commitment  to leveraging digital solutions for real -
time monitoring of fuel dispensing activities. Implementing a system that alerts the 
CCPA or relevant enforcement agencies about irregularities ensures swift intervention 
and appropriate action against any violatio ns of consumer rights or unfair trade 
practices at fuel stations.   Government is working closely with relevant stakeholders 
i.e. Oil Marketing Companies and Retail Outlet Dealers for implementation of this 
recommendation effectively, fostering a fair and t rustworthy marketplace for all 
consumers.   
        
It will also be ensured that wherever possible/ required in the event of any irregularity 
in the fuel station, information/ case may be filed with Central Consumer Protection 
Authority (CCPA) for necessary action.” 
  

3 
 
1.8  The Committee had specifically recommended that in the event of irregularity in 
the fuel station, an instant alert  should go to the agency, i.e. the CCPA for its 
necessary action.  In response  thereto, the Ministry has expressed its commitment to 
leveraging digital solutions for real-time monitoring of fuel dispensing activities which 
includes implementing a system that alerts the Central Consumer Protection 
Authority (CCPA) or relevant enforcement agencies about irregularities, ensuring 
swift intervention and appropriate action against any violations of consumer rights or 
unfair trade practices at fuel stations.    The Ministry further mentioned that it is 
working closely with relevant stakeholders, such as Oil Marketing Companies  and 
Retail Outlet Dealers, to effectively implement this recommendation, fostering a fair 
and trustworthy marketplace for all consumers.    Additionally, it has been ensured 
that in the event of any irregularities at fuel stations, information or cases may be filed 
with the CCPA for necessary action.    The Committee, therefore, urge the Ministry to 
ensure the implementation of  such measures across all fuel stations nationwide to 
maximize its impact and benefit consumers on a large scale. The Committee may be 
apprised of the progress made in this direction and the final outcome accordingly. 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No. 8) 
1.9  The Committee had recommended as under: 
The Committee note that Fuel pump calibration is crucial to safeguarding the 
consumer interest and a slight variation of millilitres in the amount of fuel being dispensed 
can add up to several litres of fuel being under-dispensed or over-dispensed. The Committee 
also learn that calibration of fuel dispensing units is done once in 12 months. Also, the 
Government have come up with a unique temper proof technology for such calibration which 
involves secure and consumer-friendly technologies, such as the use of One Time Password 
(OTP) authentication systems involving fuel station operator, fuel station system and second 
operator or system and demonstrates a commitment to enhancing security and protecting 
consumers from fraudulent activities at fuel stations. To accommodate potential delays in 
remote areas with weak signal strength, the validity period of OTPs is extended to provide 
more time in remote areas to receive and input the authentication code, reducing the 

4 
 
likelihood of authentication failures. While the  OTP system significantly enhances 
accountability and security. In this regard, the Committee, therefore, recommend that the 
Government should ensure the scrupulous adherence to the OTP system and meanwhile 
explore the possibility of roping in other advanc e technology for yearly calibration of 
dispensing machines. 
 
1.10   In its action-taken reply, the Ministry has stated as under: 
 
“Government understands the importance of scrupulous adherence to the One Time 
Password (OTP) system for ensuring secure transactions and preventing fraud in 
various sectors, including fuel dispensing. Strengthening the implementation of the 
OTP system has enhanced security measures and bolster consumer trust in the 
accuracy and fairness of fuel transactions. This approach n ot only safeguards against 
unauthorized use but also ensures that consumers receive the correct amount of fuel 
for their purchases, reinforcing transparency and reliability in the fuel dispensing 
process. 
 
Government is committed to explore advanced techno logies for the yearly calibration 
of dispensing machines by adopting state -of-the-art calibration methods to improve 
the accuracy and precision of measurements, aligning with international standards 
and best practices. By leveraging advanced technology, su ch as automated 
calibration systems and remote monitoring capabilities, Government is committed to 
streamline regulatory processes and enhance efficiency in verifying and maintaining 
the accuracy of dispensing machines. These efforts shows the Government's  
dedication to modernize regulatory frameworks and embracing innovative solutions 
that benefit both consumers and industry stakeholders alike.” 
  
1.11  In response to the Committee's recommendation, the Ministry has stated that it 
has been implementing the  OTP system to enhance security measures and bolster 
consumer trust in the accuracy and fairness of fuel transactions and has expressed 
its commitment to exploring advanced technologies for the annual calibration of 
dispensing machines. This effort aims to  improve the accuracy and precision of 
measurements, aligning with international standards and best practices. Additionally, 
the Ministry is leveraging advanced technology, such as automated calibration 
systems and remote monitoring capabilities, to stream line regulatory processes and

In this regard, the Committee urge that they may be apprised of the actual steps taken

for adherence and success of the One Time Password (O TP) system for ensuring
